name: connect-service-configuration-snowflake-refresh
description: What: Re-import 'Service Configuration Snowflake' on the Main instance so it picks up the current CrewChief secrets (delete, then import: a Connect import never updates). Sequence after a credential change: connect-database-reset, this, connect-database-backup (the baseline). Why: A building block of the Connect pack; a test, setup or schedule workload runs it so its steps exist once. When: Never run directly once the pack is tested; its parents run it. Running it alone is safe only when its own Needs are met. Needs: reference values: connect/urls:ConnectBaseUrl. Success: Every step Succeeded or Skipped. If it fails: Run connect-preflight first; then open the first failed step, whose If it fails text names what to check.

inline.description: What: Delete 'Service Configuration Snowflake'. 404 means already absent. Why: Calls the Profisee or TestAuto REST API for this change or check, the same way a client would. Success: The response status is one of the expected codes (200, 204, 404). If it fails: 401 = the API key is not set on that instance yet (run connect-setup) or the secret is wrong; 404 = the record, entity or address is missing; no response = the server in the URL (connect/urls, connect/machines) is down.

What: Import 'Service Configuration Snowflake' (copied from QA 'SC_Snowflake_Enterprise', id 823c5f8e-a2e1-2374-d694-1ff622393e71). Why: Drives Connect (strategies, service configurations, batches) through its REST API for ''. Success: Connect accepts the Import call with an expected status code. If it fails: Check the Connect address (connect/urls:ConnectBaseUrl) answers and the Connect API key works; 400 or 409 usually means the object already exists or the artifact does not fit this Profisee release.
